jobs.title: Federal Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Role

Peregrine is looking for a highly organized, resourceful operator to support our work across the federal government. This role sits at the intersection of executive support, Federal operations, and customer engagement, with exposure to some of Peregrine's most important relationships and initiatives.

You'll work closely with Peregrine leadership and our Federal team to coordinate complex schedules, travel, meetings, customer visits, and events. You'll often operate around sensitive or confidential information, making judgment, discretion, and attention to detail essential to success.

We're particularly interested in people who have learned how to operate in fast-paced government environments. You may have supported a Member of Congress or congressional committee, worked within a federal department or agency, or developed similar experience working closely with government stakeholders.

If you're someone who knows how to keep a complicated schedule moving, coordinate across many different stakeholders, anticipate what needs to happen next, and stay composed when plans change, you'll likely thrive in this role.

Responsibilities:

- Build and improve processes for scheduling, travel, events, and Federal engagements as Peregrine continues to grow.

- Jump into special projects and operational needs across the Federal organization as they arise.

- Manage complex calendars and scheduling for senior leaders, including meetings with federal customers, government officials, executives, and other external stakeholders.

- Coordinate meetings and engagements involving multiple government and internal stakeholders, navigating changing schedules and competing priorities.

- Track follow-ups, action items, and operational priorities coming out of important meetings and engagements.

- Manage domestic and international travel and the logistics  surrounding sensitive or high-priority engagements.

- Prepare leaders for upcoming meetings, travel, and events by ensuring materials, logistics , and relevant context are organized in advance.

- Handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and good judgment.

- Serve as a reliable point of contact for Federal stakeholders and their staff, ensuring requests and follow-ups are handled thoughtfully and efficiently.

- Coordinate Federal customer events, including Demo Days, customer fly-ins, executive visits, dinners, and other in-person engagements.

- Own event logistics  from start to finish, including invitations, attendee tracking, meeting spaces, catering, transportation, materials, and day-of execution.

- Partner with Sales and Marketing to create thoughtful, well-organized experiences for Federal customers and stakeholders.

What We Look For

- 5+ years of experience in government, operations, scheduling, executive support, government affairs, or another fast-paced, high-trust environment.

- Experience working on Capitol Hill, with a congressional committee, within the Executive Branch or a federal department or agency, or in an organization that works closely with the federal government.

- Experience coordinating across multiple stakeholders and managing schedules, meetings, events, or other operational priorities.

- D iscretion when handling confidential or sensitive information.

- An understanding of the norms and protocols involved in working with government officials and their staff.

- Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to keep track of many moving pieces at once.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including an ability to synthesize meetings and complex information into clear takeaways.

- A proactive mindset - you anticipate  what needs to happen rather than waiting to be told.

- Ability to stay composed and resourceful when schedules change or unexpected issues arise.

- Willingness to work across traditional functional boundaries, from managing an executive calendar to coordinating a customer dinner or running a Demo Day.

$109,000 — $127,000 USD

jobs.title: GTM Finance Lead
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Role

As GTM Finance Lead, you will be the finance partner to Peregrine's go-to-market organization, including Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Deployment. You will own the analysis that connects pipeline to bookings, bookings to ARR, and ARR to revenue and cash, and you will bring rigor to how we plan, measure, and pay for growth across public-sector and commercial segments. This role sits at the center of some of our most consequential questions: how we define and report ARR, how we price and package, how we compensate the sales team, and where we deploy our next GTM dollar. You will report to the VP of Finance and partner closely with the Controller, Revenue Operations, and GTM leadership.

What You'll Do

- Own the GTM financial model, including capacity planning, quota setting, pipeline coverage, and bookings and ARR forecasts by segment (SLG, Federal, and Commercial)

- Establish and govern clear definitions for bookings, CARR, NCARR, and ARR, including treatment of option years, consortium contracts, and escalators, and reconcile these across Salesforce, contracts, and the finance model

- Partner with Revenue Operations and the Controller to build a single source of truth for contract and ARR data

- Build unit economics by segment and channel, including CAC, payback, win rates, sales cycle length, net dollar retention, and marketing ROI

- Support pricing and packaging decisions with rigorous analysis of customer value drivers and margin impact

- Deliver a weekly and monthly GTM operating cadence that holds leaders accountable to plan and surfaces risks early

Who You Are

- 8+ years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, or GTM finance at a high-growth B2B software company, ideally with an analytical foundation in banking, consulting, or private equity

- Deep fluency in SaaS and enterprise GTM metrics, with hands-on experience building capacity models, quota plans, and ARR forecasts

- Strong data skills: you are comfortable in Salesforce reporting and SQL or equivalent, and you build your own analyses rather than waiting on others

- Credibility with sales leaders: you can push back on a forecast or a comp exception and keep the relationship intact

- AI-native, with examples of how you have automated recurring reporting or analysis

- Exceptional communication, with the ability to turn complex GTM data into a clear recommendation for executives

- Experience with government contracting, long procurement cycles, or consortium and multi-agency contracts is a strong plus

The Role

We're hiring for our Business Operations & Strategy team. In this role, you'll partner with leaders and teams across product, engineering, delivery, and revenue teams to improve operations, launch new initiatives, and help take the company to the next level. Our model is service-oriented: good ideas are often cheap, while execution, trust, and culture are everything. We work on everything from corporate strategy to day-to-day tactics, always in service of Peregrine and its people.

Our goal is to build better leaders and operators, then support them as they pursue their next direction, whether at Peregrine or elsewhere. This is not an up-or-out team; we see experience in Business Operations & Strategy as a foundation for future opportunities.

What You’ll Do

- Partner with leaders and teams across Peregrine, from deployment teams to the leadership team and CEO. You will work on challenges that are important to continued company growth but have not yet become urgent.

- Work closely with a team or business area, build a deep understanding of it, and deliver early wins. Long-term efforts rarely start with a plan or proposal; they start by building momentum and trust with the people you will partner with.

- Deliver significant operational change in whatever way the problem requires: build a model, run an operation, perform the job, bring people to agreement, or hire your replacement. Solve the problem, set it up to scale, and work closely with the people involved throughout.

- Move into other roles when it is right for you. Projects may last a few weeks or a few months; over time, you will work across the business and build conviction about the career path you want to pursue. We celebrate teammates who move into other roles as a sign of success.

- Learn, grow, and support your teammates. Our number-one rule is that team members take care of one another; we focus on growth and celebrate our teammates' success and self-development.

What We’re Looking For

- Relevant experience, ideally combining management consulting, investment banking, or private equity with work in high-growth, startup-like environments.

- Examples of delivering meaningful results. We care more about this than where you have worked: show how you have built expertise in an area of your work, navigated a startup environment, and contributed positively within and outside your team.

- You communicate complex ideas simply, identify what matters most, and help people align around a shared direction.

- You use Excel to analyze information and inform decisions. Experience using SQL, Python, and artificial intelligence tools is a plus.

- You identify opportunities, take responsibility for moving work forward, and follow through on the actions needed to solve problems.

- You can introspect, consider multiple perspectives, internalize and act on feedback, and take care of the team and others.

jobs.title: Compensation Lead
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Role

Peregrine is looking for a Compensation Lead to architect and run the programs, frameworks, and analytics that support our people through every phase of growth. This role owns compensation strategy, job architecture and leveling, compensation cycles, equity programs, and compensation analytics—and partners closely with Talent Acquisition, People, Finance, and company leadership on how we pay, level, and reward people as we scale.

This is a build-and-run role. You'll design the compensation philosophy, build the job architecture and leveling framework, own our merit and compensation review cycles end-to-end, and give recruiters, HRBPs, and managers the tools they need to make confident pay decisions. You'll also build the analytics muscle that surfaces market competitiveness, band positioning, and pay equity before anyone has to ask. As Peregrine grows, you'll have the opportunity to expand your scope and shape how the compensation function evolves.

What You Will Do

- Scale the philosophy and framework. Assess Peregrine's existing compensation programs, data, and decision-making processes, and recommend a roadmap that supports growth from roughly 500 to 1,500+ employees. Refine and document a compensation philosophy covering market competitiveness, internal equity, and the roles of base, bonus, and equity. Establish principles for market data, peer groups, and geographic positioning, and translate them into repeatable guidelines for hiring, promotions, and merit decisions.

- Build the job architecture. Design and implement a company-wide job catalog, job families, career tracks, and leveling criteria. Reconcile the new architecture with existing departmental frameworks, and partner with functional leaders, HRBPs, and Talent Acquisition to validate and drive adoption. Establish compensation bands backed by market benchmarks and internal equity principles.

- Own the compensation cycles. Run Peregrine's merit and compensation review process end-to-end—including planning, modeling, guidelines, manager inputs, approvals, communications, and post-cycle analysis. Build promotion, off-cycle adjustment, and retention award processes that scale with headcount growth. Partner with Finance to model costs and budgets.

- Enable recruiters and managers. Build tools and guidance so recruiters can self-serve the compensation inputs they need to construct and close offers. Define offer-setting guidelines and manager enablement materials. Establish a clear escalation process for exceptions, and use feedback to keep programs useful and understandable.

- Drive analytics and controls. Build compensation metrics and reporting that give People, Finance, and leadership visibility into market competitiveness, band positioning, and pay equity. Own survey participation and benchmarking cadence. Run recurring pay equity, comp-ratio, and offer-outcome analyses, and turn findings into recommendations.

- Evolve equity programs. Build the framework for new-hire, promotion, and refresh equity grants, balancing attraction and retention against dilution and affordability. Help candidates, employees, and managers understand equity as part of total compensation through clear tools and communication.

- Support executive- and board-level compensation. Develop market-informed points of view on executive compensation and prepare clear, defensible analyses for leadership and board discussions in partnership with People and Finance leadership.

About You

- You easily move between strategic design and hands-on execution—you can architect the framework and also build the spreadsheet.

- You’re an effective influencer and listener — able to bridge the world between new Peregrine systems around comp and job families, and the messy, on-the-ground reality of differing departmental contexts, dynamics, and stages of maturity.

- You’re adaptable and flexible, able to think about what will worst best for Peregrine from first principles, while still balancing that with best practices and uncompromising focus on results.

- You partner effectively with recruiters, HRBPs, executives, and board members by communicating clear, well-supported compensation recommendations.

- You have experience creating programs and infrastructure from the ground up and improving existing processes as needed.

- You assess ambiguous situations and determine when a formal program is warranted versus when a pragmatic, lighter-weight solution will work.

- You're comfortable turning messy data into a clean analytical model and translating insights into clear recommendations.

What We Look For

- 7+ years of progressive experience in compensation, with direct ownership of compensation strategy, job architecture, and program design.

- Experience building compensation infrastructure through significant headcount growth, ideally in technology or other high-growth environments.

- Deep expertise in equity compensation, market benchmarking, and job leveling.

- Strong command of HR and compensation systems and data.

- Located in San Francisco and able to work in the office 4 days/week.

jobs.title: Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Lead, Federal
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

Our Team

At Peregrine, we build software to power critical decision-making for public safety and emergency response organizations. These organizations use our technology to protect lives, protect property, and deliver their best service to the public.

We are motivated to help institutions solve their hardest problems through better decision-making. We are passionate about creating cutting-edge, highly scalable data platforms that enable organizations to transform the way they interact with their data.

As a team of service-oriented entrepreneurs, we trust each other, help each other, and dive into challenges together. We each strive to be empathetic, curious, inclusive, brave, and exceptional in our execution. Our customers are our partners; we listen to their needs, learn from their experiences, and develop effective software solutions to help them achieve transformational outcomes for their communities. Further, our team is advised by leading experts and practitioners in emergency management, justice, and civil liberties. These experts ensure we develop technology that is both operationally effective and trust-enhancing.

Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local governments, federal agencies, and private-sector institutions turn complex and disconnected data into operational intelligence. Our platform supports mission-critical decisions in environments where security, availability, data protection, and customer trust are imperative.

As Peregrine expands our work with federal customers, we are building the security and compliance capabilities necessary to operate some of our most sensitive deployments.

The Role

We are looking for a senior Governance, Risk, and Compliance leader to own Peregrine's FedRAMP High program and establish the security and compliance foundation required to support Department of War (DoW) deployments at DoD Impact Level (IL) 4, IL5, and IL6, ICD 503 accreditation for Top Secret environments, and agency-specific system authorizations.

This is not a generalist compliance or audit-support role. You will translate federal and defense requirements into implementable technical and operational controls and work across Security, Engineering, Product, Legal, Federal Deployment, and GTM to guide those controls through assessment, authorization, and continuous operation as Peregrine's federal business evolves.

Clearance and eligibility.  You currently hold, or are able to obtain, an active U.S. security clearance (required), and are based in Washington, D.C.

Our Washington, D.C. office is located in the Dupont Circle neighborhood, and this role is expected to be hybrid, with 4 in-office days per week.

What You’ll Do

- Own Peregrine's FedRAMP High authorization program — sustaining and expanding our existing ATO through continuous monitoring, remediation, and reauthorization, including Peregrine's transition from FedRAMP Rev. 5 toward applicable FedRAMP 20x requirements.

- Translate FedRAMP, NIST, federal agency, DoW and Intelligence Community requirements into technical and operational controls and establish the control architecture necessary to support IL4, IL5, and ultimately IL6 deployments alongside ICD 503 environments.

- Lead agency-specific system authorizations, from initial engagement through ATO issuance and ongoing sponsorship.

- Partner with Security and Infrastructure Engineering to evaluate system boundaries, Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM), network security, encryption and key management, logging, vulnerability and configuration management, hardening, supply-chain security, and incident response against federal and DoW requirements.

- Lead authorization artifacts, control implementation statements, evidence, assessment responses, and continuous-monitoring deliverables while ensuring documented controls are supported by architecture, configuration, automation, procedures, and operating evidence.

- Drive assessment findings and control gaps to closure and develop scalable control ownership, evidence collection, monitoring, and compliance-automation practices that improve the efficiency and quality of Peregrine's assurance program.

- Ensure external security representations accurately reflect implemented controls and evidence, and advise Peregrine's Federal and customer-facing teams during procurements, technical evaluations, security reviews, and customer engagements.

About You

- You are comfortable operating as a senior individual contributor with broad organizational influence and can drive programs across engineering, security, product, legal, operations, and customer-facing teams.

- You approach compliance as an engineering and risk-management discipline and are willing to challenge weak implementations, unsupported assertions, and inadequate evidence.

- You can turn complex or evolving requirements into defensible implementation strategies and communicate technical security issues clearly to engineers, executives, assessors, customers, and government security officials.

Preferred Certifications

- 10+ years of experience in information security, GRC, security assurance, or cybersecurity risk management, including personally leading significant portions of obtaining and maintaining FedRAMP High authorization for a cloud service provider (CSP) with one or more cloud service offerings (CSOs).

- Expertise in FedRAMP program management and federal Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementation through assessment, authorization, and remediation, plus at least two years of continuous monitoring — including 3PAO or government assessor engagement, authorization-package development, POA&M and accepted-weakness remediation, and agency or Authorizing Official engagement.

- Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 and SP 800-37, FedRAMP, the DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide, DoD cybersecurity risk management (RMF and the successor Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct), DISA SRGs/STIGs, applicable FIPS requirements, control overlays, and federal assessment and authorization practices.

- Technical understanding of cloud security architecture, including hands-on experience with AWS or AWS GovCloud, Kubernetes or containerized environments, Infrastructure as Code, and modern CI/CD.

- Experience designing sustainable compliance operations, including control ownership, evidence and weakness management, continuous monitoring, change management, and machine-readable assurance evidence such as OSCAL.

- Experience advising customer-facing teams through federal procurements, technical evaluations, and customer security reviews.

- An active or recently active U.S. government security clearance and U.S. citizenship.

Bonus Points

- Direct experience establishing and maintaining DoD IL4, IL5, or IL6 environments.

- Experience with ICD 503 accreditation and the authorization of National Security Systems, classified systems, or cross-domain solutions.

- Experience supporting federal or defense customers in environments involving CUI or other sensitive government information.

- CISSP, CISA, CGRC, CISM, CCSP, or comparable security certifications.

jobs.title: US Public Sector Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Role

We're hiring a Public Sector Compliance Manager to manage Peregrine's public sector compliance function as we grow in the U.S. market. This is a critical, highly cross-functional role for a detail-oriented operator who understands how compliance programs work in practice — not just on paper. You will be the company's owner for Peregrine’s public sector contractor obligations, building and running the systems, processes, and relationships that keep Peregrine compliant with its obligations as a government contractor. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational discipline and project management skills, as well as the ability to coordinate across multiple cross-functional teams, including Legal, People Operations, Finance, Contracts, and GRC.

What You'll Do

- Compliance Program Management

- Own our public sector compliance program — audits, FAR reps & certs, SAM.gov registrations, and contract-level obligations tracking across all active contracts

- Proactively spot compliance gaps and partner with Legal and Contracts on remediation and new contract onboarding

- Run our compliance training program end-to-end, from delivery to auditable recordkeeping

- Facility Clearance & Personnel Security

- Serve as our primary point of contact with DCSA to establish and maintain Peregrine's facility clearance (FCL)

- Manage the full personnel clearance lifecycle — investigations, determinations, reinvestigations, and records — partnering with People Ops on cleared-employee onboarding/offboarding

- Ethics & Conflicts of Interest

- Administer our ethics hotline, case tracking, and reporting to Legal and leadership

- Run our conflict of interest disclosure process and political contribution logging under FAR ethics requirements

- Support upkeep of our Code of Business Ethics and Conduct

- Vendor & Subcontractor Compliance

- Lead pre-award due diligence on subcontractors and vendors, including debarment/exclusion checks

- Maintain vendor compliance records and partner with Procurement on FAR/DFARS flow-down clauses

What We Look For

- 5+ years of experience in public sector compliance, contract administration, or a closely related field — you have seen the full compliance lifecycle and know where the landmines are

- Deep working knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and DFARS, including representations and certifications, mandatory disclosure rules, and clause flow-down requirements

- Hands-on experience with SAM.gov registration and maintenance, CAGE codes, and entity validation processes

- Experience managing facility clearances (FCL) and/or personnel security clearances in a government contractor environment; familiarity with DCSA/DSS processes preferred

- Demonstrated ability to build and operate compliance tracking systems and comfort owning a compliance calendar, managing obligation logs, and driving cross-functional accountability without being the most senior person in the room

- Experience administering ethics and compliance programs, including hotline intake, training programs, and COI processes

- Excellent project management skills with a high degree of ownership; you can manage multiple concurrent workstreams across different stakeholder groups without dropping the ball

- Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate complex regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for cross-functional stakeholders

- A natural collaborator who builds trusted relationships across Legal, People Ops, Finance, GRC, and Contracts; your ability to work cross-functionally is central to your success in this role

- JD or other legal training is not required and is not a substitute for operational compliance experience

- Located in Washington, D.C. and open to working in our office 4x/week

Annual Salary + Benefits + Equity (if applicable) + Bonus (if applicable)
$140,000 — $175,000 USD

Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, certifications or licenses, and specific work location. Information on the benefits offered is  here .

Peregrine Technologies is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We celebrate diversity and are a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.
